rows.evidence: Q1: Methods, Performance and Error Analysis, Application to Drip Irrigation Problem sections <U+2013> the authors run their own 1D Richards-equation and axisymmetric HYDRUS-2D simulations (220 and 156 runs), train self-organizing-map neural networks on the resulting feature vectors, and report MSE of SOM versus numerical model (Figs. 4, 5, 7, 8).
rows.notes: The study develops and tests a neural-network (SOM) tool that returns the trickle irrigation application time needed to reach a desired wetted depth/radius for a given initial soil moisture. It does not quantify any reduction in irrigation water applied or any water-conservation outcome, and it contains no comparison against a conventional schedule. Its only validation is SOM output versus HYDRUS-2D/1D model output (model-to-model); the only link to measurements is Meshkat et al.'s (1999) prior lysimeter validation, which is cited work, not the authors' own. The study therefore supports only a precondition (a method to compute application time) of the claimed water-saving effect. The '<U+00B1>1 cm' deviation and MSE values are validation errors of the ANN, not dispersion of a water-saving result.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods, Performance and Error Analysis, Application to Drip Irrigation Problem sections <U+2013> own numerical flow-model runs and SOM neural-network training/testing with reported MSE (Figs. 4, 5, 7, 8).
rows.notes: The study contains no crop, yield or crop-production data of any kind; the objective function is purely a target wetted soil volume (horizontal/vertical extent of saturation) for a given initial soil moisture. The ANN output is compared only with numerical model output, not with measurements from a real cropped system. It supports at most the precondition that a neural network can determine application timing, not any effect on yield.

notes: Full text appears complete (pp. 287-297). The paper is a methodological/computational study: a SOM neural network trained on simulated wetting patterns (1D Richards model for sensitivity analysis; axisymmetric HYDRUS-2D replicating Meshkat et al. 1999 for the application case). No field or laboratory measurements of its own, no water-use or yield outcomes; the only real-system validation referred to is Meshkat et al.'s lysimeter experiment, which is cited rather than the authors' own result.
